rules: Roles are policies, not replacement provider runtimes.
No second orchestration engine or duplicate thread history.
Opening a client or reconnecting must not create agents or re-enable paused policy.

proposedArchitecture.choice: Upstream-first source tree with cohesive Pulse-owned modules and a small explicit integration patch set.
alternatives: Direct edits throughout upstream: simpler initially, more recurring conflict sites.
Separate companion process/application: stronger source isolation, but duplicates lifecycle/auth/state and complicates cross-client integration.
rules: Preserve upstream file paths and ownership.
Prefer modules inside existing packages; create new packages only for real dependency or reuse needs.
Sequence shared contracts and runtime integration before independent UI work.
Extract a seam only to remove recurring conflicts or isolate important behavior for tests.
Track every upstream integration edit and its compatibility test.
Do not promise zero upstream edits or automatic forward compatibility.

clientCompatibility.webDesktop: Pulse-owned controls composed into existing thread, composer and settings patterns; no redesign decided.
clientCompatibility.releasedMobile: No assumption that we can ship new native screens or fields. Preserve tested upstream thread behavior; unsupported Pulse management stays in responsive web.
clientCompatibility.responsiveWeb: Proposed complete Pulse control path on phones, including visibility and stop/pause controls.
wireRules: Keep the baseline protocol compatible with pinned client fixtures.
Do not assume optional fields or unknown union variants decode safely.
Pulse extension messages require explicit compatible-client opt-in; otherwise keep them off shared streams.
Capabilities default to unsupported when absent; authorization is enforced on the server.
Reuse environment authentication and routing, including remote/relay/tunnel; no localhost assumptions.
gates: Pinned upstream mobile client with Pulse server.
Pulse web/desktop with baseline upstream server, with Pulse controls unavailable.
Reconnect, multi-environment switching, pause/cancel and permission enforcement.
Capture actual client versions and unsupported cases; no blanket future-client guarantee.

nextAction: Discuss pending features, starting with role autonomy and usage visibility. No runtime implementation until feature and architecture decisions are settled.

decisionPolicy.pending: Recommendations are proposals, not approval to implement.
decisionPolicy.inherit: Retain upstream behavior; port only a demonstrated missing Pulse behavior.
decisionPolicy.buildGate: Finish feature and packaging decisions, then review minimal desktop and mobile-web visuals before runtime implementation.
